headline.en: Herders called across valleys with a voice that flips, and the flip is already in yours. Listen for the jump: yours will do this too. The app hears the jump in pitch, not which voice made it: you'll hear that part yourself.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
Never a crack, never a slam back down: medium volume, land at speaking volume
Tightens, tickles or hurts: rest. Don't yodel when ill, and see someone if hoarseness lasts more than two weeks

text.en: Slide up and down once on a quiet "oo", following the ribbon. Somewhere your voice may jump: that's your flip. Go only as high as feels easy, and keep the top light, never louder.
Breathe, then once more, the same way. Two jumps in the same place make sure it's your flip.
A higher siren, twice up and down, lighter still, like an owl's hoo: many voices, often men's, flip higher. If yours already jumped twice in the same place, sing it gently or skip it.
Now on purpose: from below your flip, jump over it and back, then your first yodel hook, "yo-hee-o", twice. Listen, then sing it back.

measures.en: Scored on the flips and the notes. If the top sounded the same as the bottom, let it tip over: lighter, quieter, hootier. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: hear your two voices.

headline.en: Your voice has two sounds: chest voice, low and speaking-like, and head voice, high, light and hooty. A yodel flips between them.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
Chest buzzes
Head floats, light and quiet

text.en: Find "ho" low in chest voice, then "hoo" up high, light. Each note waits until you find it.
Hold "ho" in chest voice, easy and low.
Now "hoo", light and easy, above your flip: 4 beats. If your voice cracks on the way, you found it; a light voice may waver a little, and that's fine.

measures.en: Scored on your last "hoo" being on its note, not how steady it was: a new head voice wavers. Next: hear a flip from a slide.

text.en: Sing "ho" then "hoo" once more, and hear yours beside the guide's.

questions.en: Did the "hoo" sound like a different, lighter voice?
Did the "ho" buzz, and the "hoo" float?

headline.en: A yodel flips: the voice jumps straight from one note to the other. A slide passes through every note in between. Your ear can learn the difference.

detail.en: Straight across: a light flick
A siren between the notes

title.en: Listen as often as you like

detail.en: Only your first answer counts

text.en: Listen to both, then choose.

why.en: A jumped straight across each way. B slid through the notes between.
B went straight across. A glided, like a siren.
Over an octave the slide is long and easy to hear: B.
A smaller leap, so a slide is shorter. B still jumped straight across.

prompt.en: Which one slid only on the way down?

why.en: A flipped up, then slid down. The way down is the one singers often smear.
B flipped up and down. A slid on the way up.

measures.en: Scored on the rounds you got right first time. Next: four hooks in time.

headline.en: Four hooks in rhythm. First slowly, with a gap after each; then four in a row.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
Let the top tip over, never a hard catch
Back down at speaking volume

text.en: Two hooks at your own pace first.
Listen, then sing two hooks back, a gap after each.
Now four, in time over the home chord, a breath after the second.

measures.en: Scored half on clean flips, up and down, and half on the notes. About five minutes of flips at a time: take a break. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: open below, narrow above.

text.en: Sing the hook once more, then hear yours beside the guide's. The app hears the jump in pitch, not which voice made it.

questions.en: Did the top sound like a different, lighter voice?
Did the way down land lightly, at speaking volume?

headline.en: Yodelers switch vowel at the flip: an open vowel on the low chest note, a narrow one on the high head note. It helps the voice tip over.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
Open, then narrow
"ee" up high can pinch

text.en: Trace the yodel: the ribbon jumps straight up and back. Jump with it, light at the top.
Listen, then sing "yo-hee-o" back.
And "lo-ee-o".
The guide sings two hooks, then drops out: breathe, then sing two more, in time. Just listen to the guide's two.

measures.en: Scored on clean flips and the notes. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: the way down.

headline.en: The way down is the flip singers often slam. Never slam: land in chest voice lightly, at speaking volume, as if you'd just said "oh".

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
High to low, one flip
Speaking volume, never a thump

text.en: Over an octave first: "hee-o", landing lightly.
Over a fifth, the smallest leap: flip down, don't slide.
Listen, then sing three "hee-o"s back, each landing lightly.

measures.en: Scored on the downward flips and the notes. Listen back: did each one land lightly? Did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: different leaps.

headline.en: The same flip across different leaps: a sixth, then an octave (often easier), then a fifth, the smallest and hardest.

detail.en: You've sung a lot of flips: a minute's quiet, then a gentle warm-up
The octave gives the voice room to tip over
Small leaps tempt you to slide

text.en: The three leaps at your own pace first: a sixth, an octave, a fifth.
A sixth: listen, then sing it back.
A fifth, the hardest. Flip, don't slide.
Now all three in a row: a sixth, an octave, a fifth.

measures.en: Scored on the flips and notes across all three leaps. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: call across the valley.

headline.en: Herders called across valleys with a yodel, and the valley carried it, so you never need to push: medium volume.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
Then answer it
One hook, then two, then three

text.en: The first call: one hook.
Two hooks.
Three hooks, in time, a breath after the second.

measures.en: Scored on clean flips and the notes across all three hooks. Take a break. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: yodeling on the chord.

text.en: Sing the hook once more, then hear yours beside the guide's. The app hears the jump in pitch, not which voice made it.

questions.en: Did the top sound like a different, lighter voice?
Did the way down land lightly, at speaking volume?

headline.en: A yodel sounds right when both its notes belong to the chord underneath. As the chord changes, the top note moves with it.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
The top lands on mi
It moves up a half step, to fa

text.en: The hooks at your own pace, over the chords: the top moves up a half step on the second.
Two hooks over the home chord: listen, then sing them back.
Listen, then sing the four hooks back as the chords change.

measures.en: Scored on the flips and the notes: did the top move with the chord? Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: a cowboy lope.

headline.en: Cowboy yodels sway: long, short, long, like a horse's easy lope. The quick top note still flips cleanly.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
"yo-" held, "hee" quick, "o" held
The rhythm does the work

text.en: The lope at your own pace: long, short, long.
Listen, then sing two lopes back.
Four in a row, over the chords.

measures.en: Scored on the flips and the notes. Listen back: did it sway? Did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: hear whether a yodel fits.

headline.en: Over a chord, a yodel's top note either belongs or rubs. Hear the difference before you sing it.

detail.en: The top is one of the chord's notes
One note off, and it clashes

title.en: Listen as often as you like

detail.en: Only your first answer counts

text.en: Listen to both, then choose.

why.en: A's top was mi, a note of the chord. B's was a half step lower and rubbed.
Over this chord the top moves up to fa: B. A went a half step too far and rubbed.
A's top was fa over the home chord: it wants to fall to mi.
B's fa belongs to this chord. A's top was a half step off it.
This time the low note was off: A's chest note was a half step above sol.
A's top moved up to fa when the chord changed. B's went a half step too far and rubbed.

measures.en: Scored on the rounds you got right first time. Next: a real tune with a yodel tag.

headline.en: A cowboy song with a yodel tag: sing the line plainly, then yodel after it, open below and narrow above.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
"And the skies are not cloudy all day"
"yo-hee-o", "lo-ee-o", with the vowel switch

text.en: The line at your own pace first.
The line, plainly, over the drone.
Now the tag: listen, then yodel it back, open below and narrow above.

measures.en: Scored on the tag's flips and notes. Take a break. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: the roll.

text.en: Sing the hook once more, then hear yours beside the guide's. The app hears the jump in pitch, not which voice made it.

questions.en: Did the top sound like a different, lighter voice?
Did the way down land lightly, at speaking volume?

headline.en: A roll is several flips on one breath: low, high, low, high, low. Four flips at most to a breath.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
Each flip clean before it's quick
Never more than four flips a breath

text.en: The roll at your own pace first: low, high, low, high, low.
Listen, then sing the roll back, slowly.
A little quicker.
The same roll over the home chord, every flip clean.

measures.en: Scored on the four flips and the notes. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: faster.

headline.en: The same roll at three speeds. Keep every flip clean; if they start to smear, stay at the speed before.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
Three rungs
A smeared fast roll is a slide

text.en: The roll at your own pace first.
The roll at 60: listen, then sing it back.
At 76.
At 92. Clean, not rushed.

measures.en: Scored on the flips at 92. If they smeared, the roll at 76 is still a yodel. Listen back: did the top sound lighter, like a different voice? Next: hear a clean roll from a smeared one.

headline.en: Fast, a roll either flips cleanly or smears into slides. The clean one sparkles; the smeared one sounds like a siren.

detail.en: Each note distinct, even when quick
Glides between, no flips

title.en: Listen as often as you like

detail.en: Only your first answer counts

text.en: Listen to both, then choose.

why.en: A's notes stayed distinct. B glided between them.
B flipped every time. A smeared.
Faster still, and B slid: no clean flips.
B smeared every other flip. A stayed clean at speed.
Only A's first flip slid, but that's enough to hear.
One smeared flip in the middle of B's roll.

prompt.en: Which roll smeared only at the end?

why.en: A started clean and smeared as it went: the way tiredness shows.

measures.en: Scored on the rounds you got right first time. Next: a yodeled song.

detail.en: A lip trill or a quiet siren, up and down
"From this valley they say you are going"
Clean, at the speed you can keep clean

Now the tag: a hook and a roll. Listen, then yodel it back.
